description:
We are a dedicated 5-member team (Data Science, Backend, UI/UX, Business Analysis, Engineering & Presentation) tackling the "Planet X and SPHEREx" challenge.

Our project, SPHEREx-EYE, is an AI-powered platform processing SPHEREx’s 102-band infrared data to detect Planet X, asteroids, and celestial anomalies in seconds. We combine deep learning, backend architecture, and UI design to deliver an interactive NASA-level solution for space exploration and citizen science.
summary:
SPHEREx-EYE is an interactive web prototype that transforms multi-epoch sky imagery into actionable space-mission decisions. While existing astronomical tools flag moving sources, translating a raw coordinate shift into an operational flight decision still requires slow manual triage.

We developed a fast, three-step pipeline using FastAPI, OpenCV, and Astropy. First, it aligns archival NASA SkyView FITS plates taken decades apart to detect moving candidates via blink comparison and residual differencing. Second, it cross-matches detections against ESA Gaia DR3 astrometry and evaluates a simulated 102-band infrared spectral model (0.75–5.00 µm) to estimate temperature, velocity, and ice absorption indicators (H₂O at 3.00 µm, CH₄ at 3.32 µm, and CO₂ at 4.27 µm). Third, it generates a one-page Astronaut Object Dossier with a hazard level and recommended next action, exportable as a printable PDF mission report or JSON file.

By turning sky data into clear mission decisions in under two seconds for cached sectors, SPHEREx-EYE accelerates candidate triage for mission planners while making NASA data accessible in any browser.
details:
What It Does & How It Works:

SPHEREx-EYE is a web-based astronomical detection and mission-triage prototype that bridges the gap between raw sky imagery and operational spacecraft decisions. Built around a three-step automated pipeline—Detect, Analyze, and Decide—the platform runs end-to-end in under two seconds for cached sky sectors:

1. Detect: Users select a sky sector (such as Barnard’s Star, Kapteyn’s Star, Proxima Centauri, Pleiades, or Sedna) or upload two custom FITS/image plates. Our backend fetches multi-epoch archival plates (e.g., 1953 Palomar DSS1 Red vs. 1996 DSS2 IR), aligns them using 2D phase correlation (cv2.phaseCorrelate) and affine warping, normalizes brightness ranges, and isolates moving candidates through blink comparison and residual difference mapping.

2. Analyze: Each detected candidate is cross-matched live against ESA Gaia DR3 (proper motion, parallax, G magnitude) and evaluated with a simulated 102-band infrared Spectral Energy Distribution (SED) model (0.75–5.00 µm) to estimate surface temperature, tangential velocity, signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), and ice absorption signatures (H₂O at 3.00 µm, CH₄ at 3.32 µm, and CO₂ at 4.27 µm).

3. Decide: Instead of stopping at raw coordinates, SPHEREx-EYE generates a one-page Astronaut Object Dossier for every candidate—complete with a hazard classification (LOW / Nominal, MODERATE / Trajectory Monitor, or HIGH / Delta-V Avoidance), recommended next actions, and one-click printable PDF Mission Report (via browser print layout) and JSON/CSV exports.

Benefits & Intended Impact:

- Accelerates Candidate Triage: Saves astronomers and mission planners hours of manual blink inspection by pairing astrometry, spectral modeling, and hazard logic in one interface.

- Democratizes Space Data: Allows students, educators, and citizen scientists to inspect real multi-epoch NASA FITS plates directly in a web browser without specialized desktop software.

- Maximizes Mission Value: Prepares a ready-to-plug-in decision layer designed for NASA’s 102-band SPHEREx all-sky survey releases.

Tools, Languages & Software Used:

- Backend & Scientific Computing: Python 3.10+, FastAPI, Astropy (WCS coordinate projections & FITS handling), Astroquery, OpenCV (cv2 phase correlation, morphological filtering & contour pairing), NumPy, and SciPy.

- Frontend & Visualization: HTML5, Tailwind CSS, JavaScript, Chart.js (interactive 102-band SED plots), and browser print-to-PDF mission dossier generation.

Creativity & Key Design Factors Considered:

- Operational Decision Layer: Most sky viewers stop at showing pixels; we designed SPHEREx-EYE from the perspective of a flight-operations engineer who needs an immediate risk level and recommended action.

- Reliability & Speed: To prevent browser lag or external server hangs during live sessions, we engineered local FITS caching, single-WCS reuse, bounded local SNR windows, and a three-tier offline fallback mechanism.

- Scientific Honesty & Explainability: We deliberately used transparent, rule-based astrophysical thresholds rather than a black-box model, clearly distinguishing real archival imagery and live Gaia queries from our simulated 102-band SED prototype.
